answer: At dawn a real person signs one standing mandate naming one address as the only party that may ever speak for them, their shop and their name, and a sprig of juniper marks the sealing. A head clears an epoch only when a mandate names it. The scarce per-head input is one person's real agency: a farm's tenth head needs a tenth person to bind their livelihood to an address they cannot check, and the roll of mandates pulses once per name, so one address holding a column of other people's authority teaches honest people to stop signing. A mandate is spent on use, never lent to a sibling head.
